findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O failure (missing file, permissions, disk error)
findings.failure_mode: entire program aborts on any filesystem error instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, std::io::Error> and use ? to propagate the error

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric second field
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line aborts the entire batch instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: use .map_err() to convert ParseIntError into a domain error and propagate via Result

findings.problem: Lossy `as u16` cast on parse::<u32>() result — silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: values in 65536..=u32::MAX silently wrap to 0..=65535, producing incorrect data with no error
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parts[1].parse::<u32>()?) and propagate OverflowError as a typed domain error

findings.problem: Unchecked indexing `parts[0]` — no bounds check before access
findings.failure_mode: empty or single-element lines panic with index-out-of-bounds

findings.problem: Unchecked indexing `parts[1]` — no bounds check before access
findings.failure_mode: lines with only one field panic with index-out-of-bounds

findings.problem: Uses `split(',')` + `map` + `collect` into `Vec<String>` when a line has exactly two fields
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation of Vec<String> for every line; allocates more parts than needed
findings.fix: use `split_once(',')` to extract the two fields directly without intermediate allocation

findings.problem: I/O side effect (`println!`) inside a data-parsing iterator
findings.failure_mode: parsing logic is no longer pure/deterministic; side effects leak into the data pipeline and cannot be tested in isolation
findings.fix: remove `println!` from the iterator; logging belongs in the imperative shell layer, not the core parser

findings.problem: I/O (`fs::read_to_string`) is mixed into the parsing pipeline — no boundary between shell and core
findings.failure_mode: the function does both file I/O and parsing, making the pure parsing logic untestable in isolation
findings.fix: split into two functions: `load_text(path: &str) -> Result<String, io::Error>` in the shell, and `parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>` in the core

findings.problem: `Record.value: u16` is a raw primitive — any u16 value (including 0) is valid, even if domain rules forbid it
findings.failure_mode: invalid domain states (e.g., value=0) are representable and not rejected at compile time
findings.fix: use a newtype `Value(u16)` with a fallible constructor that enforces domain invariants

findings.problem: `Record.name: String` is a raw primitive — empty strings are valid, even if domain rules forbid it
findings.failure_mode: empty names are representable and not rejected
findings.fix: use a newtype `Name(String)` with a constructor that rejects empty/whitespace-only input

findings.problem: Function returns `Vec<Record>` with no bounded capacity handling — no `try_reserve` or capacity checks
findings.failure_mode: unbounded memory growth from large files; no allocation-failure handling
findings.fix: compute capacity from line count or use `try_reserve` before collecting; map allocation failure to a typed error

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sessions throughput or memory usage
no profiler data (flamegraph, perf, or cprofile) for allocation hotspots
no allocation audit (e.g., `tracy`, `dhat`, or `valgrind --leak-check`) for the Vec<String> per-line allocation pattern
no command-bounded CLI entry point — no evidence of how the function is invoked with validated arguments
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The code has multiple BLOCKER violations: unwrap on I/O and parse, lossy as cast, unchecked indexing, mixed I/O in parsing pipeline, and unnecessary allocations. All unwrap() and as-cast usages must be replaced with typed error propagation before any delivery gate can pass.
